analysis.title: PREVIEW - US October jobs data is due on 6th November 2026 at 13:30GMT/08:30EST
key_insights: Consensus expects October nonfarm payrolls of +63k (vs 29k in September), against a three-month average of 51k, a six-month average of 66k and a 12-month average of 41k.
Unemployment rate is expected to hold at 4.2%. The Chicago Fed's final estimate is 4.14% vs 4.18% for September, citing more hiring and fewer layoffs.
Average hourly earnings are expected at +0.3% M/M (prev. 0.1%) with the annual rate easing to 2.9% Y/Y from 3.0%, the first sub-3% reading since May 2021.

Labour market proxies were largely positive: initial claims in the survey week were 195K (vs 198K in the September window), continuing claims 1.701mln (vs 1.712mln), and ADP private payrolls rose 86K vs 69K expected.
Challenger October job cuts were 43,994, up 2% M/M, down 71% Y/Y and the lowest October since 2023. AI was cited for 1,265 cuts, the lowest monthly total this year.
Challenger hiring plans were 444,692, up 57% Y/Y and the highest October since at least 2009, but dominated by seasonal roles (Amazon 300K, UPS 100K).
Revelio's public data showed 26K jobs added in October vs a revised 67.6K in September, a slowdown in job growth.
September JOLTS were strong: openings rose 333K to 7.523mln (exp. 7.1mln), layoffs fell 127K to 1.641mln (lowest since March 2025), and quits rose 321K to 3.365mln, the largest rise since May 2023.
ISM manufacturing employment fell 0.3 points to 52.4 (fourth month in expansion). ISM services employment rose 1.3 points to 51.4, with hiring breadth mixed (six industries up, seven down).
Conference Board labour differential widened 2.4 points to +5.3, and net six-month jobs expectations rose 1.8 points to -11.1.
Money markets price about an 83% chance of a 25bps Fed hike in December to 4.00-4.25%. Analysts say a consensus-like print lets the Fed stay focused on inflation.

risk_factors: ADP is usually a poor guide to any single month's official print, with an average absolute gap of 77K to the first private payrolls estimate since August 2022 (Pantheon).
Revelio's data pointed to slower job growth in October (26K vs a revised 67.6K in September).
Hiring breadth in the ISM services survey was mixed, with seven industries reporting a decrease in employment.
Challenger hiring plans were dominated by seasonal roles, with employers favouring short-term hiring over permanent headcount.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive proxies (claims 195K, ADP 86K, strong JOLTS, ISM services employment 51.4) support a solid print, and a consensus-like result lets the Fed stay focused on inflation and hike in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Revelio showed only 26K jobs added, ADP is a poor guide to the official print (average gap 77K), and Oxford Economics puts payrolls at 40K with break-even near 25K.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A payroll print well below the 63k consensus, or a rise in the unemployment rate above 4.2%, would weaken the case for the December hike.

theme_stances.key_argument: A consensus-like jobs print allows the Fed to stay focused on inflation and raise rates in December.
